transformations.edit: Replaced the seed string recorder with an executable Verus function whose body is the Rust 1.96 target body `IterMut::new(slice)`, adapting only the inherent `[T]` receiver to an explicit `slice: &mut [T]` parameter and naming the return.
Attached the generated iterator-view and final mutable-slice frame postconditions to the target function; this records the contract under test and does not assume the target body.

Represented `IterMut` in the harness by its lifetime marker while assigning Rust's private `ptr: NonNull<T>` and `end_or_len: *mut T` fields, ZST length encoding, and pointer provenance to the `IterMut::new` boundary. The target body never inspects those fields.

Modeled the private callee `IterMut::new` as an external-body boundary with the exact source-backed postconditions needed by the target delegation: iterator source and remaining sequence equal the old slice, empty yielded prefix and remainder, forward direction, and no immediate mutation of the slice view.
